cards.h: Why you can digest a roti
cards.b: Without help, digesting starch would take years. Your body does it in hours because of enzymes, biological catalysts that speed reactions up millions of times. Lactose intolerance, fever, food spoilage and many medicines all come down to enzymes.

Nearly all enzymes are proteins (some RNA). An enzyme lowers the activation energy, the push needed to start a reaction, and is not used up. It acts on a substrate at a pocket called the active site.

Analogy: a key and lock. Better: a glove that tightens around the hand (induced fit, Daniel Koshland, 1958).

1. Temperature: rises with heat until the enzyme folds out of shape (denatures).
  2. pH: pepsin works at pH 2, trypsin near 8.
  3. Substrate amount: speed rises then levels off when all enzymes are busy (Michaelis and Menten, 1913).
  4. Inhibitors: block the active site or bend the enzyme.

Many enzymes need helpers. Metal ions like zinc or magnesium are cofactors. Small organic helpers are coenzymes; many are made from vitamins, such as NAD from niacin (B3). That is why vitamin lack causes disease.

Cells link reactions into chains. The product of one enzyme is the substrate of the next. Often the final product switches off the first enzyme, called feedback inhibition, like a tap that closes when the tank is full.
Cells pay for work using ATP (adenosine triphosphate). Breaking its last phosphate releases usable energy. A person turns over about their body weight of ATP each day, recycling it from ADP.

Eduard Buchner showed in 1897 that yeast juice without living cells could ferment sugar (Nobel 1907). James Sumner crystallised urease in 1926 and showed it was a protein. Many doubted him until others confirmed it.

Fix these

  • Cold does not kill enzymes; it slows them. Heat can destroy them.
  • Enzymes do not supply energy; they lower the hill to climb.
  • Enzymes are not changed permanently by reactions.

Curd, idli and dosa batter, and toddy rely on microbial enzymes. Lactase persistence varies across Indian populations, so lactose intolerance is common in many regions. Statin drugs and many cancer drugs work by inhibiting key enzymes.

• Enzymes lower activation energy and are reusable.
  • Speed depends on temperature, pH, substrate, inhibitors.
  • Pathways are tuned by feedback inhibition.
  • ATP is the cell's energy coin.

Think about it:

  1. Why does fever above about 41 C become dangerous?
  2. Why might a drug that mimics a substrate block an enzyme?
